newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT-Australia 10-yr bond eyeing the peak.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Australia 10-yr bond eyeing the peak.

text.p: The September Australian 10-year bond futures contract will be looking to test last Monday's 93.090 peak this week as this month's steep rising trendline remained intact during afterhours trading.
The contract ended SYCOM at 93.000 compared with Friday's 92.925 pit close, helped along by a late rally in the U.S. Treasury market.

Initial resistance is seen at 93.015, the market's previous peak set in December, before it tries to take out the 3-1/4 year high of 93.090 set by the now expired June contract, and then aims for a target of 93.180, analysts said.
Initial support is seen at 92.950 and then 92.880 before the market retests last week's 92.845 low.

Speculation of a further monetary policy easing after the July 1 Reserve Bank board meeting will retain an underlying bid tone, although the market is again likely to suffer from another extremely thin data week.

The September bill futures contract has roughly priced in a 50 basis points easing in current official 5.5 percent interest rates, ending SYCOM four basis points higher than its open outcry close at 94.90, and pointing to a cash rate of 5.10 percent. --Colin Brinsden 61-2 9373-1800
